references.title: The Will to Believe, and Other Essays in Popular Philosophy
references.edition: New York: Longmans, Green, and Co., 1897 [c1896]

collation_findings.direction: 1912 Project Gutenberg transcription checked against 1897 first-edition LoC witness
collation_findings.method: Word-level alignment against LoC's scan-derived OCR, followed by targeted checks around the live/dead, forced/avoidable, momentous/trivial definitions, genuine-option definition, Pascal discussion, and concluding permission.
collation_findings.result: No confirmed substantive change was found in the target essay's argument or the benchmark-critical formulations. Non-matches were dominated by LoC OCR errors, running headers/page numbers, hyphenation, and front/footnote material; examples include live->zve and option->oftion. The ingested artifact remains identified as the 1912-impression Gutenberg transcription, not silently relabelled as the 1897 text.
collation_findings.limitations: This is not a new critical edition and does not authorize the LoC OCR as semantic evidence. Any later claimed wording difference must be checked directly against the page image before freeze.
